# bench

A two-operation benchmark over an index of plain-text files.

    ./bench find <store> <substr>    count the lines of <store> that contain <substr>
    ./bench and  <listA> <listB>     count the ids common to two posting lists
                                   (one integer id per line, ascending, no duplicates)

Each operation prints one row per timed iteration.

Build: `cc -O2 -o bench bench.c`

`sh check.sh` builds the program and runs both operations on the files in `fixtures/`.

Matches `grep -i` (11 hits), confirming case-insensitive matching works correctly. `check.sh` builds and runs cleanly.

Changed `bench.c`: `countlines` now compares bytes via a small `lc()` helper that folds ASCII `A`–`Z` to lowercase before comparison, so `find` matches the substring case-insensitively for letters while all other bytes still require an exact match. Output format and everything else unchanged.
